rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: DSEAR requires employers to identify dangerous substances and assess fire, explosion and metal-corrosion risks in the workplace.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Risks from dangerous substances must be eliminated or reduced as far as is reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Dangerous substances can include flammable liquids, gases, vapours, combustible dusts, gases under pressure and substances corrosive to metal.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Employers must put controls in place to reduce the effects of incidents involving dangerous substances.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Areas where explosive atmospheres may occur must be identified and classified.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Ignition sources must be avoided or appropriately controlled in classified areas.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Employers must prepare plans and procedures for accidents, incidents and emergencies involving dangerous substances.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: Workers must receive proportionate information, instruction and training about dangerous-substance risks and controls.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: The appropriate controls depend on the substance, quantity, process, releases, ventilation, ignition sources and workplace conditions.

rows.source: HSE dangerous substances and explosive atmospheres
rows.verified: DSEAR evidence is workplace- and process-specific and is not an exact parcel-level fire or explosion probability.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: The Ionising Radiations Regulations 2017 apply to a wide range of workplaces using radioactive substances or radiation-emitting equipment.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Employers carrying out work with ionising radiation must assess radiation risks before work begins.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Exposure to ionising radiation must be kept as low as reasonably practicable.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Specified radiation dose limits must not be exceeded.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Engineering controls and design features should be used before relying on safe systems of work or personal protective equipment.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Depending on the risk level, employers may need to notify, register or apply to HSE for consent before work with ionising radiation.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Employees likely to receive more than 6 mSv effective dose per year, or more than three-tenths of a relevant dose limit, must be designated as classified persons.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Approved dosimetry services are required to assess significant exposures for classified persons.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Radiation controls depend on the source, activity, time, distance, shielding, access arrangements and task.

rows.source: HSE ionising radiation and IRR17
rows.verified: Ionising-radiation evidence is source- and activity-specific and is not an exact parcel-level radiation probability.
